whatis.intro: Material markup is the percentage added to what goods cost you, to set their selling price. The term is common in contracting, where materials are marked up on a job. For a distributor the material is the case, costed all the way to your dock.

cards.title: Everything it takes to reach your dock
cards.body: Everything you pay to get the case onto your dock and ready to ship: the supplier price, freight in and handling. The markup goes on top of that total.
cards.alt: Plus sign, for the costs that land a case on your dock

cards.title: Overhead stays out of the case
cards.body: Rent, sales pay, insurance and the office. They belong to the business, not the case, so the margin the markup leaves has to pay for them.
cards.alt: Minus sign, for overhead the margin has to cover

cards.title: Freight in, not freight out
cards.body: The $1.40 to bring a case in is part of its cost. The truck that takes it to your account is a cost to serve, and it comes out of margin.
cards.alt: Warning sign, for inbound freight against delivery to the account

who.h2: Who uses a material markup calculator
who.intro: A distributor that buys product in and resells it by the case needs a true case cost before any markup goes on. Anyone who builds a case cost, sets the markup rule or tracks freight should run it.

look.h2: Where a material markup leaks margin
look.intro: The markup is the one number you choose. Freight, handling and shrink are estimates, and estimates are where the margin goes wrong.

steps.title: Freight split over what really arrived
steps.body: A load charge divided by a full truck's worth of cases understates freight when the truck came half full. Divide by the cases that arrived.

steps.title: Handling from timed work, not a guess
steps.body: Time a few pallets from the dock to the shelf, and cost the hours at the full wage with taxes. Then divide by the cases.

steps.title: Shrink from your own write-offs
steps.body: Use the credits and write-offs in your own books, not a rule of thumb. The 3% default is a starting point, and perishables can run higher.

vos.h2: Where VOS fits after the markup
vos.h3: A markup only holds on the right line
vos.body: VOS does not calculate your costs or set your markup. Its part comes after the price: customers order by voice in the VOS app and check each line before they send it.
